season.evidence: No stored season. A glaciated, bivy-based alpine line on the north side; summit ascents on this peak are Jul 57, Aug 43, Sep 10, Oct 2 (all routes). Web search found no modern beta for this line, only the standard southwest route, which Mountaineers lists for Jul-Sep; the north glacier approach is best after snow has consolidated, so Jul-Sep.

season.evidence: Stored Jul-Oct stands. Logged ascents: Jul 57, Aug 43, Sep 10, Oct 2. Web search: Mountaineers lists the Storm King southwest route for Jul-Sep; guide pages give mid-August as the typical date; early July still has deep snow in the basin.

track.why: 3 Jul 2026 summited track (4 m from our summit pin). The report describes the usual climber's traverse to the correct notch below the summit, the exposed ledge catwalk and a roped step up the summit crack, matching our route's Hazard pins (north-side ledge traverse, summit crux crack). The track starts at High Bridge, runs over Park Creek Pass and out Thunder Creek to end 39 m from our Colonial Creek pin, so it is a through-trip; all three approaches are named in our text. Mechanical oneway test is false (start is 30 km from our pin) and the report says half of day one is missing; owner/script should decide if a through-trip is acceptable. 3 Jul is in season.

otherTracksConsidered.why: 9 Aug 2025 from the Goode high camp at ~2,250 m, partial, double-peak trip; no trailhead.
2 Aug 2025 42-mile trip whose highest point is on Goode, 1.2 km from this summit.

facts.text: In early July the Park Creek trail and the climber's path above it pass through a burn with hundreds of blowdowns; allow far longer than normal for the approach.
In early July the high bench near 7,400 ft is still under snow with no running water; melt snow, and expect soft snow on the traverse to the notch.
Snow can fill the moat along the ledge past the catwalk in early July; one party stemmed between snow and rock, then climbed a steep, roughly 100 ft class 4+ pitch that needed protection.
Rappel slings were found chewed by animals in late July; inspect or replace all tat, and do not trust the second anchor, a loose boulder resting on other loose rocks.
Take the right-hand gully to the summit ledges; the horn-topped gully to its left is a dead end with loose rock. Late-August parties found downclimbing the northeast ledges easier than rappelling.
60 m rope (a 70 m avoids a short downclimb after the last rappel), small cams, and slings for anchors (Jul-Aug)
Camp water is available at about 6,300 ft where waterfalls drain, if the drainage near 5,600 ft is dry; the traverse from the 7,400 ft bench to the notch is half talus, half snow in late July.

notes: The summit pin matches Peakbagger's surveyed coordinate (22 m). No pin changes needed. The track 3255971 is a through-trip; use only if the owner accepts oneway-through-trip recordings (the mechanical oneway test was false). A 2017 report warns a guidebook photo mislabels the summit, which can send parties up a wrong gully.
